rulings.challenge_claim: The unit's load-bearing structural warrant -- an infinitive purpose chain running unbroken to the unit's own close -- is not what the pointed bytes carry, and the finite-clause differentia used to place the seam at Isa.61.4 is already met one clause earlier, inside this span.
rulings.grounds: The finding is byte-true; the account of HOW the chain breaks is partly not, so this refines rather than upholds flat. UPHELD, and it is the load-bearing half: oshb:Isa.61.3 runs 24 tokens; token 17 is כֵּהָ֑ה carrying the verse's main caesura, and token 18 opens וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ (byte tier), a waw-plus-perfect finite clause; the row's own quoted closing word לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier) is token 24, inside that finite clause. The row's warrant, that the purpose chain 'runs without a finite-verb break through the unit's own close', is therefore byte-false at the unit's own close. UPHELD with a correction: וּבָנוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier) is the same waw-plus-perfect construction, so that construction is not unique to the seam verse -- but the row's stated differentia is a finite THIRD-PERSON-PLURAL clause, and the 61:3b verb is not third-person-plural, so the criterion is not identically satisfied inside the span; only its finite-clause half is. NOT UPHELD, the framing leg: מָשַׁח֩ and שְׁלָחַ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Isa.61.1, byte tier) do not 'break' the chain twice. The row names the sending as the chain's GOVERNOR, and all six infinitives after it follow it; counting the governing perfects as breaks reads against the row's own claim rather than against it. UPHELD, the re-tiering leg, and it is the second real defect: לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.60.21) and לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3) are byte-identical (sweep: 2 verses book-wide for that form), while the planting nouns are not -- oshb:Isa.60.21 stages the ketiv/qere pair מטעו מַטָּעַ֛י (unpointed ketiv beside pointed qere, byte tier) against oshb:Isa.61.3's מַטַּ֥ע (sweep: 3 verses on that consonantal string, skeleton tier: oshb:Isa.14.19, oshb:Isa.60.21, oshb:Isa.61.3). The row's device_notes calls the pair a 'collocation' and a 'catchword' with NO tier label at all, which is precisely the tier-disclosure standard's failure mode, and the apparatus doubling at the earlier verse is not disclosed either. NEW FINDING (neither lens): the paseq inventory records 1 seg at MT 61:3, inside this row's own span, undisclosed, while sibling rows in these clusters do disclose their span-relevant paseq. The unconditional span-relevant symmetry sweep covers the parashah layer, not paseq, so this is a disclosure-consistency gap rather than a validator failure -- recorded at low weight. The anointed-speaker hold is untouched and stays open: no eved-root token stands in oshb:Isa.61.1-Isa.61.3 (sweep: 0 eved-root tokens over the unit's 3 verses), the challenge does not contest the hold, and this ruling does not decide it.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace 'runs without a finite-verb break through the unit's own close' with a formulation that names the waw-plus-perfect opening oshb:Isa.61.3's second half after the caesura, and state the seam differentia as the SUBJECT change (the mourners named in the impersonal-passive clause at 61:3b against the third-person-plural community at 61:4), not as the presence or absence of a finite verb. device_notes: tier-label the catchword -- byte-identical only at the 'to be glorified' form, the planting nouns skeleton-level and ketiv/qere-doubled at oshb:Isa.60.21 -- quoting each spliced form; and add the span-interior paseq disclosure at MT 61:3 (count-only, single-witness, no position asserted). TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): re-read oshb:Isa.61.3's 24 tokens and confirm no field asserts an unbroken infinitive chain through the unit's own close, since the row's own quoted closing word sits inside a finite clause; and re-collate the catchword pair against each other, not only each against its own verse, so the tier named is the collate result. No span change, no unit_type change, and the servant-referent hold is not author work.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: this unit's own opening simile reuses, at the accent-stripped tier, the garland word that closes the anointed speaker's commission three verses earlier -- an undisclosed recurrence bearing on the very speaker question the row leaves open. OL: two undisclosed lexical hooks in the opening verse reach back across the front seam into both preceding units, and the close rests on the chapter division plus a genre contrast rather than on anything the bytes mark.
rulings.grounds: The two items share ONE core defect and each adds one distinct leg. SAME DEFECT, upheld: the garland non-disclosure. פְּאֵ֜ר (oshb:Isa.61.3, token 6, byte tier) against פְּאֵ֔ר (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier) differ only in cantillation and are identical at accent_stripped tier; the standalone token stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier, oshb:Isa.61.3 and oshb:Isa.61.10). Both lenses tier it correctly and the row discloses it nowhere. Under the cross-seam cohesion rule a byte-true device reaching across the row's own front seam argues continuity unless disclosed, and here it is not neutral texture: the row's device_notes leaves open whether the rejoicing voice is 'the same figure who speaks beginning at Isa.61.1', which is exactly what the garland tie bears on. OL's asymmetry point is also correct and aggravating -- the unit opening at 61:1 disclosed the catchword at its OWN edge while this one discloses none. DISTINCT leg (OL), REFINED inside this uphold: the priest-root hook is a real ROOT echo -- כֹּהֲנֵ֤י (oshb:Isa.61.6, byte tier) against יְכַהֵ֣ן (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier) -- but OL's framing and digit are defective. The two tokens do not carry 'the same consonants'; only the three-letter root is shared. Swept per attested spelling, the 61:10 verb form stands in exactly 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier) and the 61:6 noun form in 4 (sweep: 4 verses, skeleton tier: oshb:Isa.10.15, oshb:Isa.37.2, oshb:Isa.61.6, oshb:Isa.66.21) -- and that 4 blends the priest noun with a preposition-plus-verb string at oshb:Isa.10.15, a contiguous-substring false hit of exactly the class the hazard catalogue names. So 'sweep: 4 verses for each attested spelling' is wrong for one spelling and count-object-blended for the other; the leg survives only as a root echo across a two-verse gap and carries far less weight than the garland tie. DISTINCT leg (OL), upheld: the back seam. The row's closing sentence ends 'closing this unit at the chapter division', and chapter divisions are tier-4, never boundary evidence. The residual rhetorical-mode contrast is real, but the first-person-singular voice runs straight across the seam -- שׂ֧וֹשׂ אָשִׂ֣ישׂ (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier) against לֹ֣א אֶחֱשֶׁ֔ה and לֹ֣א אֶשְׁק֑וֹט (oshb:Isa.62.1, byte tier) -- and that continuity is undisclosed. NEW FINDING (neither lens): 1 paseq seg stands at MT 61:11, inside this row's own span, undisclosed -- the same disclosure-consistency class recorded on P17-002 at MT 61:3, and again not a validator failure. The speaker's identity stays open; this ruling does not decide it.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: add the garland disclosure -- splice the noun from oshb:Isa.61.3 and oshb:Isa.61.10, name the tier as accent_stripped (byte differs by cantillation), name the swept object (standalone token, 2 verses book-wide), and state explicitly that the tie is disclosed continuity that does NOT resolve the held speaker question; add the span-interior paseq at MT 61:11 (count-only, single-witness). boundary_rationale: delete 'at the chapter division' and re-ground the back seam on the rhetorical-mode contrast alone, disclosing that the first-person-singular voice runs across the seam into oshb:Isa.62.1. If the priest-root echo is carried at all, carry it as a ROOT echo with per-spelling digits (verb form 1 verse; noun form 4 verses, one of them a substring false hit) and never as 'the same consonants'. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: re-run the cross-seam cohesion read over oshb:Isa.61.3-Isa.62.1 and confirm no byte-true or accent-true device straddling either of this row's edges is left unnamed, and that every digit written names its swept object. No span change; the unit_type deviation disclosure already in device_notes stays.

rulings.challenge_claim: The seam is carried by an 'explicit vocative' and a 'new first-person divine act' at Isa.62.6 that the bytes do not supply, while the second-feminine-singular addressee runs straight through it.
rulings.grounds: UPHELD on all three legs, with one qualification on the first. Leg 1: oshb:Isa.62.6 opens עַל חוֹמֹתַ֣יִךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם (byte tier) -- the city name stands in apposition with no vocative particle or marker. QUALIFICATION: Hebrew vocatives are ordinarily unmarked, so the defect is not that an address is impossible but that the row calls it EXPLICIT and treats the naming of the addressee as a CHANGE of addressee. Leg 2, and this is the load-bearing one: the addressee is continuous across the claimed seam. This unit's own last two words are עָלַ֖יִךְ אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ (oshb:Isa.62.5, byte tier, 2fs) and the first suffixed word of the next verse is the 2fs form in עַל חוֹמֹתַ֣יִךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם -- the same addressee either side. OL's suffix census re-derives correctly at accent-stripped tier (oshb:Isa.62.2 three tokens, 62:3 one, 62:4 six, 62:5 four, 62:6 one, 62:7 none, 62:8 three), and the address carries on past the following seam at דְּגָנֵ֨ךְ, לְאֹ֣יְבַ֔יִךְ and תִּֽירוֹשֵׁ֔ךְ (oshb:Isa.62.8, byte tier). So the row's stated ground -- an opening 'that this unit's own address to Zion does not share' -- is byte-contradicted. Leg 3: 'new first-person divine act' fails on both qualifiers. oshb:Isa.62.1 already carries לֹ֣א אֶחֱשֶׁ֔ה and לֹ֣א אֶשְׁק֑וֹט (byte tier), so the person is not new. On the 'divine' half the challenge is right but its wording is byte-false and needs correcting -- and the corrected form is stronger for it. The divine name is NOT absent from Isa.62.1-Isa.62.6: it stands in 4 of those 6 verses (sweep: 4 verses carrying the tetragrammaton over the 6-verse stretch -- oshb:Isa.62.2, oshb:Isa.62.3, oshb:Isa.62.4, oshb:Isa.62.6 -- beside the suffixed 'your God' at oshb:Isa.62.3 and oshb:Isa.62.5). What is true, and decisive, is that EVERY one of those occurrences is THIRD person relative to the first-person voice, including inside the seam verse itself, where the addressed group is told to remind הַמַּזְכִּרִים֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier). So the first-person speaker is nowhere identified with the named deity, and the divine attribution at the seam verse is inference -- the unnamed-speaker class a chunking row should hold rather than drive a seam with. NEW FINDING (neither lens): the row's own front-portion sentence, that 'the same second-person address to Zion runs through the renaming and marriage imagery', starts one verse late. oshb:Isa.62.1 carries no second-person token at all; Zion is referred to in the third person there -- צִדְקָ֔הּ וִישׁוּעָתָ֖הּ (byte tier, 3fs suffixes). The 2fs address begins at oshb:Isa.62.2. This is an independent defect in the row's own internal description and it strengthens the continuity finding. CONFIDENCE: the row records high. With both named differentiae byte-contested and the residual seam signal reduced to the introduction of a participant group inside a continuous addressee and a continuous voice, high is not carried by the bytes. Not challenged and confirmed: the ketiv/qere handling at oshb:Isa.62.3 stages both forms side by side, and the parashah-absence statement is inventory-correct (segs stand at MT 61:9 and MT 62:9, none between).
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative: strike 'an explicit vocative' and 'a new first-person divine act' as the seam's differentiae; re-ground the seam on what the bytes do carry -- the introduction of a new participant group (posted watchmen) and the shift of the speaker's own act from vow to appointment -- and ADD the disclosure that both the 2fs addressee and the 1cs voice run across the seam. Correct the front-portion sentence: the second-person address begins at oshb:Isa.62.2, not at the unit's opening verse, which speaks of Zion in the third person. confidence: lower from high (a row-field change, not a respan), and mirror the row into the sidecars with a bespoke why_low_confidence naming the unmarked-seam problem. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: re-run the addressee-suffix read over oshb:Isa.62.1-Isa.62.8 and confirm no field states a differentia that is satisfied on BOTH sides of this row's own seam. No span change proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: The cohesion argument and the rejected alternative both attribute the 'give no rest' summons to the watchmen, but in the bytes that summons is addressed to them by the same speaker who posted them.
rulings.grounds: UPHELD, byte-confirmed and load-bearing. The second half of oshb:Isa.62.6 reads אַל דֳּמִ֖י לָכֶֽם and oshb:Isa.62.7 opens וְאַֽל תִּתְּנ֥וּ (both byte tier): both are addressed second-person-plural forms, and the English witness reads the same way. No petition is uttered BY the watchmen anywhere in Isa.62.6-Isa.62.9; the commands are laid ON them by the speaker who posted them. The row's 'The watchmen's own summons' and its rejected alternative's 'the watchmen's own petition' therefore name a speech role the bytes do not attest -- a speech-role misassignment of exactly the class the campaign's role-split discipline exists to catch. The defect is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: the ONLY stated ground for not splitting at the oath verse is that 'the sworn content answers the watchmen's own petition'. Remove the petition and the rejected alternative is left undefeated, so the row's rival disclosure is empty as written. OL's second leg is upheld and is the sharper half: the addressee alternates inside the span -- 2fs in עַל חוֹמֹתַ֣יִךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם (oshb:Isa.62.6), 2mp at אַל דֳּמִ֖י לָכֶֽם and וְאַֽל תִּתְּנ֥וּ (oshb:Isa.62.6-Isa.62.7), 2fs again at דְּגָנֵ֨ךְ and תִּֽירוֹשֵׁ֔ךְ (oshb:Isa.62.8), all byte tier -- and it is undisclosed in a row whose FRONT-seam argument turns on an addressee shift. That asymmetry, not the label alone, is what makes the item medium. NEW FINDING (neither lens): the same misattribution PROPAGATES. P17-007's boundary_rationale and its strongest_rejected_alternative both re-use 'the watchmen's own petition' / 'the watchmen's own intercession', so the corrected speech role must be swept across both rows in one edit rather than spot-fixed here. Not challenged and confirmed: נִשְׁבַּ֧ע יְהוָ֛ה (oshb:Isa.62.8, byte tier) does open the oath-negative construction running to the unit's close, and the setumah at MT 62:9 is inventory-true, correctly typed, single-witness, and the only span-relevant parashah seg (sweep: 1 parashah seg over the span's 4 Masoretic verses).
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cast the speech role -- the imperatives at MT 62:6b-62:7 are addressed TO the posted watchmen by the speaker, not uttered by them. Restate the cohesion argument as the oath answering the charge the speaker lays on the watchmen, and give the rejected split at the oath verse a ground that survives that correction. device_notes: disclose the 2fs / 2mp / 2fs addressee alternation inside the span with spliced tokens and tier, since an addressee shift is the row's own front-seam driver. Apply the identical speech-role correction to P17-007's two fields in the SAME edit -- seam-pair cures are one edit and symmetry completion is a sweep, not a spot fix. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: re-read oshb:Isa.62.6-Isa.62.7 and confirm no field in either row attributes a petition, summons or intercession to the watchmen as SPEAKERS, and that the rejected alternative still has a ground once the misattribution is gone. No span change.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the closing rationale leans on an unnamed chapter-spanning renaming bracket without citing the recurring form that carries it, and never weighs the rival that the same bracket argues for one larger bracketed unit across the chapter. OL: both edges are genuinely corroborated, but the stated onset differentia does not discriminate -- the group commanded at Isa.62.10 is the group already commanded in the preceding verses -- and the bracketing claim is under-specified.
rulings.grounds: The two items overlap on one leg and diverge on two; the shared leg is upheld but needs re-anchoring, so this refines. SHARED and upheld: the bracket is asserted without naming the form. The recurring form is real -- יִקָּרֵא֙ (oshb:Isa.62.4, byte tier) and יִקָּרֵ֣א (oshb:Isa.62.12, byte tier), identical at accent_stripped tier and differing only in cantillation -- and the row names neither. LF's tiering is right, including its honest note that עֲזוּבָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.62.4) against נֶעֱזָֽבָה (oshb:Isa.62.12) is a root-level echo only, the two forms standing in different stems. REFINED, and this is the corrected finding: OL's anchor is the better one. The row says the renaming pair 'brackets the resolve opened at Isa.62.1', but that verse carries no renaming at all. What the closing renaming answers is וְקֹ֤רָא לָךְ֙ שֵׁ֣ם חָדָ֔שׁ (oshb:Isa.62.2, byte tier) together with the renaming at oshb:Isa.62.4. So the bracket is not merely unnamed -- it is mis-anchored by one verse onto a verse that carries no member of the pair. LF's 'unnamed' framing understates this and OL's 'under-specified' understates it in the other direction. REFINED (LF's rival leg): LF is right that the row never weighs the larger reading, and the bracket as RE-ANCHORED does argue it. Two things bound its force, though, so it is a disclosure duty rather than a boundary defect: whole-chapter spans cap at medium_low under the campaign rule, and the parashah layer marks BOTH of this row's own edges (setumah at MT 62:9 and MT 62:12, inventory-true, correctly typed, single-witness). Any actual respan is a boss-adoption PROPOSAL, never author work. UPHELD but downgraded to a consequence (OL's differentia leg): oshb:Isa.62.10 does open a dense addressed-plural imperative run -- עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ then פַּנּ֖וּ then סֹ֣לּוּ סֹ֤לּוּ then סַקְּל֣וּ then הָרִ֥ימוּ (byte tier), seven tokens including two doubled pairs -- but the preceding verses already command an unnamed addressed-plural group, so 'addressed to an unnamed group rather than continuing the watchmen's own petition' states a continuity as though it were a break AND inherits the speech role the bytes do not attest. This is the second instance of the P17-006 class, not an independent finding. SEVERITY: LF said medium, OL said low. Medium is right, because the bracket is mis-anchored rather than merely unnamed and because the differentia error is a propagating class -- but OL is correct that the seam itself is the best-corroborated in this stretch and is not in doubt, which is why this is a rationale cure and not a boundary question.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: name the bracket's members with spliced, tier-labelled forms (the niphal 'will be called' at oshb:Isa.62.4 against oshb:Isa.62.12, accent_stripped tier) and RE-ANCHOR the bracket to the naming clause at oshb:Isa.62.2 rather than to the resolve at 62:1; add oshb:Isa.62.2 and oshb:Isa.62.4 to boundary_evidence_refs, which currently cite neither for this claim. Correct the onset differentia under the same speech-role cure ordered on P17-006: the preceding verses already command an addressed-plural group, so the discriminator at the onset verse is the turn from a charge laid on posted watchmen to a highway-preparation summons plus the messenger proclamation at the following verse -- not 'an unnamed group'. strongest_rejected_alternative: add the disclosure that the re-anchored renaming bracket also argues a larger chapter-scale unit, recording the tier-3 setumah segs at MT 62:9 and MT 62:12 (single-witness) as the corroboration that keeps this row's own edges. The larger-unit reading is DISCLOSED, not adopted; a respan is a boss-adoption proposal and would fall under the whole-chapter medium_low cap. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: re-read oshb:Isa.62.1-Isa.62.12 and confirm every recurring form the rationale relies on is quoted with its tier and anchored to a verse that actually carries it, and that no field attributes a petition to the watchmen. No span change.

rulings.challenge_claim: The dialogue frame is real but its byte architecture is misdescribed: the doubled opening question exists only in the English rendering, the unit's genuine second question at Isa.63.2 is neither quoted nor cited, and the Masoretic apparatus claims are keyed to the wrong numbering space.
rulings.grounds: UPHELD on all three legs. Leg 1: oshb:Isa.63.1 carries the interrogative exactly once, verse-initially -- מִי זֶ֣ה בָּ֣א מֵאֱד֗וֹם (byte tier) -- while the second clause opens on a bare demonstrative, זֶ֚ה הָד֣וּר בִּלְבוּשׁ֔וֹ (byte tier), with no interrogative. The English witness supplies the question a second time. So the row's 'the prophetic voice twice opens with a vocative challenge' is translation-dependent and does not survive into the Hebrew; and 'vocative' is the wrong class in either witness -- the opener is interrogative. Leg 2, load-bearing: oshb:Isa.63.2 opens verse-initially with מַדּ֥וּעַ (byte tier), a genuine second question INSIDE the exchange. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative rejects a two-verse/four-verse split on the ground that 'no tier-1 signal marking a sub-seam' stands inside the exchange -- and a verse-initial interrogative is exactly a tier-1 candidate signal. The verse appears in neither the prose nor boundary_evidence_refs, so the rival is defeated against the one verse that most bears on it. This does NOT decide the split: the question/answer/question/answer shape can still be held as one speech event. It is the stated ground that is byte-contradicted. Leg 3: the row keys MT-inventory claims under the web: prefix -- both setumah refs and both paseq refs carry web: while the parashah and paseq inventories are Masoretic-keyed. The CONTENT is inventory-true (setumah at MT 62:12 and MT 63:6; 1 paseq seg each at MT 63:1 and MT 63:3; no intra-verse position asserted; single-witness labelled) and chs 62-63 are identity numbering, so the arithmetic is harmless here -- but the witness label is wrong, and the row sits three units upstream of the offset zone. NEW FINDING (widens leg 3 from a row defect into a class): the same web-keyed apparatus stands in P18-002, whose boundary_evidence_refs key the front-seam parashah seg, the ketiv/qere note and all three paseq segs under web: as well, while P18-004 keys its parashah claim correctly as an explicit dual. This is a writer-part pattern, so the cure is a sweep across the part, not a spot fix in one row. Not challenged and confirmed: the first-person self-identification splice re-collates at byte tier, and the dialogue-form deviation is disclosed under the operative-category rule as the closed vocabulary requires.
rulings.remedy: boundary_evidence_refs: re-key every parashah and paseq entry to the Masoretic witness (oshb:Isa.62.12, oshb:Isa.63.6, oshb:Isa.63.1, oshb:Isa.63.3) and sweep the same re-keying across the sibling rows of this writer part -- P18-002 carries the identical defect and P18-004 already shows the correct form. boundary_rationale: replace 'twice opens with a vocative challenge' with an interrogative-class description that quotes the single verse-initial interrogative and names the second clause as a bare demonstrative; add oshb:Isa.63.2 with its verse-initial interrogative to BOTH the prose and boundary_evidence_refs. strongest_rejected_alternative: re-ground the refusal to cut inside the exchange on something other than the absence of a tier-1 signal -- holding the question/answer/question/answer shape as one speech event between one pair of voices is available and byte-honest. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: re-run the prose-to-refs mirror so every verse argued in prose stands in boundary_evidence_refs, and confirm no Masoretic-inventory claim anywhere in the row carries a web: prefix. No span change.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the seam-opening claim that Isa.63.7 launches a fresh first-person-plural speaker misstates the verse's grammatical person and the row's own dominant voice. OL: the stated tier-1 onset ground misdescribes the grammatical person of the opening verb, and the phrase the row says is named twice is not the same phrase at byte tier.
rulings.grounds: The person leg is the SAME defect in both lenses on the same bytes; OL adds two distinct legs. SAME DEFECT, upheld: oshb:Isa.63.7 carries אַזְכִּיר֙ (byte tier), a first-person SINGULAR form, and the plural in that verse is an object suffix, גְּמָלָ֖נוּ (byte tier) -- matching the row's own English quotation, which has an I-subject with an us-object. 'A fresh first-person-plural speaker' is byte-false. One shared imprecision to record against both lenses: neither calls the verse correctly when it says the verb 'opens' the recital -- oshb:Isa.63.7 opens חַֽסְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה and the verb stands at token 3. It does not touch the finding. DISTINCT leg (OL), upheld and stronger than the shared one: grammatical person does not shift at the front seam AT ALL, because the preceding warrior speech is also first-person singular -- וְאָב֤וּס (oshb:Isa.63.6, byte tier). So the row's onset ground fails on both halves: the person label is wrong AND person is not the differentia. What survives, as OL says, is the self-announcing speech-act verb itself. DISTINCT leg (OL), upheld: ר֣וּחַ קָדְשׁ֑וֹ (oshb:Isa.63.10) against ר֥וּחַ קָדְשֽׁוֹ (oshb:Isa.63.11) differ at byte tier AND at accent-stripped tier -- the later occurrence carries a meteg that accent-stripping retains -- agreeing only at skeleton tier. The row labels each splice byte tier, correct for each AT ITS OWN VERSE, while calling them 'the same phrase', so the RECURRENCE claim carries no tier of its own and implies an identity the bytes do not give. That is the tier-disclosure standard's named failure mode, and OL's further observation is byte-true: both splices cut away the governing אֶת that stands before each occurrence.
